review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

15:1.sourceText: Ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ἄμπελος ἡ ἀληθινή, καὶ ὁ Πατήρ μου ὁ γεωργός ἐστιν.
15:1.targetText: “I am the true vine, and My Father is the keeper of the vineyard.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:2.sourceText: πᾶν κλῆμα ἐν ἐμοὶ μὴ φέρον καρπὸν, αἴρει αὐτό, καὶ πᾶν τὸ καρπὸν φέρον, καθαίρει αὐτὸ ἵνα καρπὸν πλείονα φέρῃ.
15:2.targetText: He cuts off every branch in Me that bears no fruit, and every branch that does bear fruit, He prunes to make it even more fruitful.

groups.note: κλῆμα is understood again with πᾶν τὸ καρπὸν φέρον, where BSB repeats branch.
Article and participle τὸ … φέρον form one unit.
καρπὸν … φέρῃ ("it may bear fruit") is rendered it … fruitful; BSB adds make.

unmappedSource.reason: The resumptive αὐτό ("it") repeats the fronted object, which English states once.
The resumptive αὐτό ("it") repeats the fronted object, which English states once.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies make in its recast; in the Greek the branch itself is the subject of φέρῃ ("bear").

15:3.sourceText: ἤδη ὑμεῖς καθαροί ἐστε διὰ τὸν λόγον ὃν λελάληκα ὑμῖν·
15:3.targetText: You are already clean because of the word I have spoken to you.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the relative pronoun ὅν ("which") unexpressed.

15:4.sourceText: μείνατε ἐν ἐμοί, κἀγὼ ἐν ὑμῖν. καθὼς τὸ κλῆμα οὐ δύναται καρπὸν φέρειν ἀφ’ ἑαυτοῦ ἐὰν μὴ μένῃ ἐν τῇ ἀμπέλῳ, οὕτως οὐδὲ ὑμεῖς ἐὰν μὴ ἐν ἐμοὶ μένητε.
15:4.targetText: Remain in Me, and I will remain in you. Just as no branch can bear fruit by itself unless it remains in the vine, neither can you bear fruit unless you remain in Me.

groups.note: μείνατε is understood again with κἀγὼ ἐν ὑμῖν, where BSB repeats remain.
κἀγώ (καί + ἐγώ) is rendered and I.
δύναται is understood again with οὐδὲ ὑμεῖς, where BSB repeats can.
καρπόν is understood again with οὐδὲ ὑμεῖς, where BSB repeats fruit.
φέρειν is understood again with οὐδὲ ὑμεῖς, where BSB repeats bear.
ἐὰν μή ("if not") together supply unless.
ἐὰν μή ("if not") together supply unless.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves οὕτως ("so") unexpressed after Just as.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies will; the Greek clause κἀγὼ ἐν ὑμῖν has no verb of its own.

15:5.sourceText: ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ἄμπελος, ὑμεῖς τὰ κλήματα. ὁ μένων ἐν ἐμοὶ κἀγὼ ἐν αὐτῷ, οὗτος φέρει καρπὸν πολύν, ὅτι χωρὶς ἐμοῦ οὐ δύνασθε ποιεῖν οὐδέν.
15:5.targetText: I am the vine and you are the branches. The one who remains in Me, and I in him, will bear much fruit. For apart from Me you can do nothing.

groups.note: Article and participle ὁ μένων form one unit.
κἀγώ (καί + ἐγώ) is rendered and I.
Greek doubles the negative (οὐ … οὐδέν); English says nothing once.

unmappedSource.reason: The resumptive οὗτος ("this one") repeats the subject, which English states once.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the clauses; the Greek has no connective here.
English supplies the verb; ὑμεῖς τὰ κλήματα has none (as the supplied am in John 14:10).

15:6.sourceText: ἐὰν μή τις μένῃ ἐν ἐμοί, ἐβλήθη ἔξω ὡς τὸ κλῆμα καὶ ἐξηράνθη, καὶ συνάγουσιν αὐτὰ καὶ εἰς τὸ πῦρ βάλλουσιν, καὶ καίεται.
15:6.targetText: If anyone does not remain in Me, he is like a branch that is thrown away and withers. Such branches are gathered up, thrown into the fire, and burned.

groups.note: BSB attaches ἐβλήθη ("was thrown") to the branch in its comparison.
The object αὐτά ("them") becomes the subject of BSB's passive.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence here instead of rendering καί.
BSB lists the verbs with a comma instead of rendering this καί.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies he is for the comparison; the Greek makes him the subject of ἐβλήθη ("was thrown").

15:7.sourceText: ἐὰν μείνητε ἐν ἐμοὶ καὶ τὰ ῥήματά μου ἐν ὑμῖν μείνῃ, ὃ ἐὰν θέλητε αἰτήσασθε καὶ γενήσεται ὑμῖν.
15:7.targetText: If you remain in Me and My words remain in you, ask whatever you wish, and it will be done for you.

groups.note: ὃ ἐάν ("whatever") works as one unit.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:8.sourceText: ἐν τούτῳ ἐδοξάσθη ὁ Πατήρ μου, ἵνα καρπὸν πολὺν φέρητε καὶ γενήσεσθε ἐμοὶ μαθηταί.
15:8.targetText: This is to My Father’s glory, that you bear much fruit, proving yourselves to be My disciples.

groups.note: ἐν τούτῳ ("in this") is rendered This, the subject of BSB's sentence.
ἐδοξάσθη ("was glorified") is rendered is to … glory.
BSB's Greek has a different form of this verb here, with the same sense.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB turns the second verb into the participle proving and leaves καί untranslated.

15:9.sourceText: καθὼς ἠγάπησέν με ὁ Πατήρ, κἀγὼ ὑμᾶς ἠγάπησα· μείνατε ἐν τῇ ἀγάπῃ τῇ ἐμῇ.
15:9.targetText: As the Father has loved Me, so have I loved you. Remain in My love.

groups.note: κἀγώ (καί + ἐγώ) is rendered so … I.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:10.sourceText: ἐὰν τὰς ἐντολάς μου τηρήσητε, μενεῖτε ἐν τῇ ἀγάπῃ μου, καθὼς ἐγὼ τοῦ Πατρός μου τὰς ἐντολὰς τετήρηκα καὶ μένω αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ ἀγάπῃ.
15:10.targetText: If you keep My commandments, you will remain in My love, just as I have kept My Father’s commandments and remain in His love.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:11.sourceText: Ταῦτα λελάληκα ὑμῖν ἵνα ἡ χαρὰ ἡ ἐμὴ ἐν ὑμῖν ᾖ καὶ ἡ χαρὰ ὑμῶν πληρωθῇ.
15:11.targetText: I have told you these things so that My joy may be in you and your joy may be complete.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:12.sourceText: αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ ἐντολὴ ἡ ἐμὴ, ἵνα ἀγαπᾶτε ἀλλήλους καθὼς ἠγάπησα ὑμᾶς.
15:12.targetText: This is My commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:13.sourceText: μείζονα ταύτης ἀγάπην οὐδεὶς ἔχει, ἵνα τις τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ θῇ ὑπὲρ τῶν φίλων αὐτοῦ.
15:13.targetText: Greater love has no one than this, that he lay down his life for his friends.

groups.note: τις ("someone") is rendered he.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:14.sourceText: ὑμεῖς φίλοι μού ἐστε, ἐὰν ποιῆτε ὃ ἐγὼ ἐντέλλομαι ὑμῖν.
15:14.targetText: You are My friends if you do what I command you.

groups.note: BSB's Greek has a different form of this relative pronoun here, with the same sense.

15:15.sourceText: οὐκέτι λέγω ὑμᾶς δούλους, ὅτι ὁ δοῦλος οὐκ οἶδεν τί ποιεῖ αὐτοῦ ὁ κύριος· ὑμᾶς δὲ εἴρηκα φίλους, ὅτι πάντα ἃ ἤκουσα παρὰ τοῦ Πατρός μου ἐγνώρισα ὑμῖν.
15:15.targetText: No longer do I call you servants, for a servant does not understand what his master is doing. But I have called you friends, because everything I have learned from My Father I have made known to you.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the relative pronoun ἅ ("which") unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:16.sourceText: οὐχ ὑμεῖς με ἐξελέξασθε, ἀλλ’ ἐγὼ ἐξελεξάμην ὑμᾶς, καὶ ἔθηκα ὑμᾶς ἵνα ὑμεῖς ὑπάγητε καὶ καρπὸν φέρητε καὶ ὁ καρπὸς ὑμῶν μένῃ, ἵνα ὅ τι ἂν αἰτήσητε τὸν Πατέρα ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου δῷ ὑμῖν.
15:16.targetText: You did not choose Me, but I chose you. And I appointed you to go and bear fruit—fruit that will remain—so that whatever you ask the Father in My name, He will give you.

groups.note: ὅ τι ἄν ("whatever") works as one unit; BSB's Greek differs slightly here, with the same sense.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the subject ὑμεῖς ("you") unexpressed in the phrase to go.
BSB replaces this καί with a dash.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves ὑμῶν ("your") unexpressed with the repeated fruit.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:17.sourceText: ταῦτα ἐντέλλομαι ὑμῖν, ἵνα ἀγαπᾶτε ἀλλήλους.
15:17.targetText: This is My command to you: Love one another.

groups.note: ἐντέλλομαι ("I command") is recast as the noun phrase My command.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB renders the ἵνα clause as a direct command and leaves ἵνα ("that") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula in its recast.

15:18.sourceText: Εἰ ὁ κόσμος ὑμᾶς μισεῖ, γινώσκετε ὅτι ἐμὲ πρῶτον ὑμῶν μεμίσηκεν.
15:18.targetText: If the world hates you, understand that it hated Me first.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves ὑμῶν ("before you") unexpressed after first.

15:19.sourceText: εἰ ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου ἦτε, ὁ κόσμος ἂν τὸ ἴδιον ἐφίλει· ὅτι δὲ ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου οὐκ ἐστέ, ἀλλ’ ἐγὼ ἐξελεξάμην ὑμᾶς ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου, διὰ τοῦτο μισεῖ ὑμᾶς ὁ κόσμος.
15:19.targetText: If you were of the world, it would love you as its own. Instead, the world hates you, because you are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world.

groups.note: BSB uses it for ὁ κόσμος ("the world") just named.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB reorders the sentence and leaves διὰ τοῦτο ("therefore") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object you and as; the Greek object is τὸ ἴδιον ("its own").

15:20.sourceText: μνημονεύετε τοῦ λόγου οὗ ἐγὼ εἶπον ὑμῖν Οὐκ ἔστιν δοῦλος μείζων τοῦ κυρίου αὐτοῦ· εἰ ἐμὲ ἐδίωξαν, καὶ ὑμᾶς διώξουσιν· εἰ τὸν λόγον μου ἐτήρησαν, καὶ τὸν ὑμέτερον τηρήσουσιν.
15:20.targetText: Remember the word that I spoke to you: ‘No servant is greater than his master.’ If they persecuted Me, they will persecute you as well; if they kept My word, they will keep yours as well.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:21.sourceText: ἀλλὰ ταῦτα πάντα ποιήσουσιν εἰς ὑμᾶς διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου, ὅτι οὐκ οἴδασιν τὸν πέμψαντά με.
15:21.targetText: But they will treat you like this because of My name, since they do not know the One who sent Me.

groups.note: Article and participle τὸν πέμψαντα form one unit.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves πάντα ("all") unexpressed in like this.
BSB makes you the direct object of treat and leaves εἰς ("to") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:22.sourceText: εἰ μὴ ἦλθον καὶ ἐλάλησα αὐτοῖς, ἁμαρτίαν οὐκ εἴχοσαν· νῦν δὲ πρόφασιν οὐκ ἔχουσιν περὶ τῆς ἁμαρτίας αὐτῶν.
15:22.targetText: If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not be guilty of sin. Now, however, they have no excuse for their sin.

groups.note: ἁμαρτίαν … εἴχοσαν ("they would have sin") is rendered would … be guilty of sin.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:23.sourceText: ὁ ἐμὲ μισῶν καὶ τὸν Πατέρα μου μισεῖ.
15:23.targetText: Whoever hates Me hates My Father as well.

groups.note: Article and participle ὁ … μισῶν form one unit.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:24.sourceText: εἰ τὰ ἔργα μὴ ἐποίησα ἐν αὐτοῖς ἃ οὐδεὶς ἄλλος ἐποίησεν, ἁμαρτίαν οὐκ εἴχοσαν· νῦν δὲ καὶ ἑωράκασιν καὶ μεμισήκασιν καὶ ἐμὲ καὶ τὸν Πατέρα μου.
15:24.targetText: If I had not done among them the works that no one else did, they would not be guilty of sin; but now they have seen and hated both Me and My Father.

groups.note: ἁμαρτίαν … εἴχοσαν ("they would have sin") is rendered would … be guilty of sin.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the first καί ("both") of καὶ … καί untranslated before have seen.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:25.sourceText: ἀλλ’ ἵνα πληρωθῇ ὁ λόγος ὁ ἐν τῷ νόμῳ αὐτῶν γεγραμμένος ὅτι Ἐμίσησάν με δωρεάν.
15:25.targetText: But this is to fulfill what is written in their Law: ‘They hated Me without reason.’

groups.note: ὁ λόγος ("the word") is rendered what.
Article and participle ὁ … γεγραμμένος form one unit.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

ὅτι introduces the quotation and has no English counterpart.

15:26.sourceText: Ὅταν ἔλθῃ ὁ Παράκλητος ὃν ἐγὼ πέμψω ὑμῖν παρὰ τοῦ Πατρός, τὸ Πνεῦμα τῆς ἀληθείας ὃ παρὰ τοῦ Πατρὸς ἐκπορεύεται, ἐκεῖνος μαρτυρήσει περὶ ἐμοῦ·
15:26.targetText: When the Advocate comes, whom I will send to you from the Father—the Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father—He will testify about Me.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:27.sourceText: καὶ ὑμεῖς δὲ μαρτυρεῖτε, ὅτι ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς μετ’ ἐμοῦ ἐστε.
15:27.targetText: And you also must testify, because you have been with Me from the beginning.
